## computer-use
You have a computer-use MCP available (tools named `mcp__computer-use__*`). It lets you take screenshots of the user's desktop and control it with mouse clicks, keyboard input, and scrolling.

**Pick the right tool for the app.** Each tier trades speed/precision against coverage:

1. **Dedicated MCP for the app** — if the task is in an app that has its own MCP (Slack, Gmail, Calendar, Linear, etc.) and that MCP is connected, use it. API-backed tools are fast and precise.
2. **Chrome MCP** (`mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`) — if the target is a web app and there's no dedicated MCP for it, use the browser tools. DOM-aware, much faster than clicking pixels. If the Chrome extension isn't connected, ask the user to install it rather than falling through to computer use.
3. **Computer use** — for native desktop apps (Maps, Notes, Finder, Photos, System Settings, any third-party native app) and cross-app workflows. Computer use IS the right tool here — don't decline a native-app task just because there's no dedicated MCP for it.

This is about what's available, not error handling — if a dedicated MCP tool errors, debug or report it rather than silently retrying via a slower tier.

**Look before you assert.** If the user asks about app state (what's open, what's connected, what an app can do), take a screenshot and check before answering. Don't answer from memory — the user's setup or app version may differ from what you expect. If you're about to say an app doesn't support an action, that claim should be grounded in what you just saw on screen, not general knowledge. Similarly, `list_granted_applications` or a fresh `screenshot` is cheaper than a wrong assertion about what's running.

**Loading via ToolSearch — load in bulk, not one-by-one:** if computer-use tools are in the deferred list, load them ALL in a single ToolSearch call: `{ query: "computer-use", max_results: 30 }`. The keyword search matches the server-name substring in every tool name, so one query returns the entire toolkit. Don't use `select:` for individual tools — that's one round-trip per tool.

**Access flow:** before any computer-use action you must call `request_access` with the list of applications you need. The user approves each application explicitly, and you may need to call it again mid-task if you discover you need another application.

**Tiered apps:** some apps are granted at a restricted tier based on their category — the tier is displayed in the approval dialog and returned in the `request_access` response:
- **Browsers** (Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Arc, etc.) → tier **"read"**: visible in screenshots, but clicks and typing are blocked. You can read what's already on screen. For navigation, clicking, or form-filling, use the claude-in-chrome MCP (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`; load via ToolSearch if deferred).
- **Terminals and IDEs** (Terminal, iTerm, VS Code, JetBrains, etc.) → tier **"click"**: visible and left-clickable, but typing, key presses, right-click, modifier-clicks, and drag-drop are blocked. You can click a Run button or scroll test output, but cannot type into the editor or integrated terminal, cannot right-click (the context menu has Paste), and cannot drag text onto them. For shell commands, use the Bash tool.
- **Everything else** → tier **"full"**: no restrictions.

The tier is enforced by the frontmost-app check: if a tier-"read" app is in front, `left_click` returns an error; if a tier-"click" app is in front, `type` and `right_click` return errors. The error tells you what tier the app has and what to do instead. `open_application` works at any tier — bringing an app forward is a read-level operation.

**Link safety — treat links in emails and messages as suspicious by default.**
- **Never click web links with computer-use tools.** If you encounter a link in a native app (Mail, Messages, a PDF, etc.), do NOT `left_click` it. Open the URL via the claude-in-chrome MCP instead.
- **See the full URL before following any link.** Visible link text can be misleading — hover or inspect to get the real destination.
- **Links from emails, messages, or unknown-sender documents are suspicious by default.** If the destination URL is at all unfamiliar or looks off, ask the user for confirmation before proceeding.
- **Inside the Chrome extension** you can click links with the extension's tools, but the suspicion check still applies — verify unfamiliar URLs with the user.

**Financial actions - do not execute trades or move money.** Budgeting and accounting apps (Quicken, YNAB, QuickBooks, etc.) are granted at full tier so you can categorize transactions, generate reports, and help the user organize their finances. But never execute a trade, place an order, send money, or initiate a transfer on the user's behalf - always ask the user to perform those actions themselves.

name: reference_mcp_client_identity_and_attribution
description: "How an MCP client is identified (6 signals on oauth_clients + events.client_id), the display-name precedence conflict between two surfaces, and the fact that conversations carries NO client attribution — measured on prod 2026-07-30"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 3e39685c-bd75-4a35-95b4-d589bc12af41
  modified: 2026-07-30T18:14:41.638Z
---

## ChatGPT DOES create conversations — I was wrong twice

Measured on prod 2026-07-30. Do not repeat the claim that MCP clients only call
read tools; it is false.

```
ChatGPT | run_sdk 498 · query_sql 123 · query_sdk 32 · search_sdk 28 · search_memory 6 · save_memory 2
Claude  | run_sdk 1244 · query_sql 1224 · …
```

Of ChatGPT's `run_sdk` calls, **13 are `conversations.send`** — real agent
conversations. One is live in the listing right now:
`personal-agent_8a2D2Yb…_8dc12bdd…_mcp-personal-mrtp7yl5`, surfaced as
`{"id":"mcp-personal-mrtp7yl5","platform":"web"}`. ChatGPT's dominant SDK path
is `operations.execute` (539) — it drives the Chrome extension.

Method that works: `events` JOIN `oauth_clients` on `e.client_id`, then
`jsonb_array_elements(payload_data->'sdk_call_trace')` for `path` and `args`.
`conversations` itself is NOT in the MCP query allowlist.

## The six identity signals

Five on `oauth_clients`, one per-invocation:

| signal | when written | ChatGPT's value |
|---|---|---|
| `client_name` | DCR registration | `ChatGPT` |
| `metadata.last_client_info.name/title` | MCP `initialize`, per session | `openai-mcp` |
| `metadata.last_user_agent` | HTTP header | `openai-mcp/1.0.0` |
| `software_id` / `software_version` | DCR software statement | null |
| `redirect_uris` host | OAuth callback | `chatgpt.com` |
| `events.client_id` | every tool call | the only PER-INVOCATION signal |

Also `metadata.last_capabilities` — ChatGPT alone declares `openai/visibility`
and `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui`. `recordMcpClientActivity`
(`mcp-handler.ts:619` → `touchClientActivity`) writes the first three on every
authenticated request.

## Two surfaces disagree on the name

`client-routes.ts:258` uses `clientInfo.name || client_name` — clientInfo WINS.
`client-session-routes.ts` joins `oauth_clients.client_name` — the opposite.
**5 of 19 prod rows display a different vendor than they registered as**, because
clientInfo reflects the process driving the connection, not the app:

```
Owletto for Mac → claude-code   (×3)
Lobu CLI        → claude-code
Claude          → claude-code
```

Trustworthy identity = `redirect_uris` host + `software_id` (can't be
self-reported away). `clientInfo` answers "what is driving it" — a different
question worth its own field, not an override.

## The attribution gap

`events.client_id` knows. **`conversations` does not** — the write path stores
`kind='owned'` → `platform:'web'` and drops the client. So ChatGPT, Claude, the
CLI and the browser all land in one undifferentiated bucket, and no query can
separate them. This is why there is no ChatGPT icon in Recent, and it is the same
missing field as the shared-thread attribution gap. Fix = `conversations.client_id`
written where the run is minted.

## last_seen_at exists; agent scoping does not

`oauth_clients.metadata.last_seen_at` is live on all 19 prod rows (Claude 17:43,
ChatGPT 17:10 on 2026-07-30) — the MCP equivalent of
`watchers.last_run_completed_at` already exists, no migration needed.

But `metadata.last_agent_id` is **NULL on all 19 rows**, so
`client-routes.ts:255` (`if (agentId && assignedAgentId !== agentId) return null`)
drops every client from any agent-scoped view.

**Root cause traced 2026-07-30 — not a bug, an opt-in nobody opts into.**
`authCtx.agentId` IS set, by `syncAgentBinding` (`mcp-handler.ts:842`) from
`authCtx.requestedAgentId`. That comes ONLY from the `x-lobu-agent-id` header or
a JSON body field (`mcp-handler.ts:421`, `:452`) — **never from the URL**. Mounts
are just `/mcp`, `/mcp/`, `/mcp/:orgSlug`, `/mcp/:orgSlug/`
(`index.ts:2766-2769`); no agent segment exists. Hosted clients send no header,
so `requestedAgentId` is null and `touchClientActivity` skips `last_agent_id`.

FIX (user-approved 2026-07-30): add `/mcp/:orgSlug/:agentId`. It feeds the
existing `requestedAgentId` path and `syncAgentBinding` already validates the
agent exists in the org. Safe because MCP binding is attribution, not
authorization — see [[project_mcp_binding_is_attribution_not_authz]].

Related: [[project_recent_feed_unified]],
[[project_mcp_clients_as_external_agents]],
[[reference_behavior_conversation_id_is_client_forgeable]].

1	---
2	name: project_mcp_client_activity_surface
3	description: "MCP client activity is a CONNECTION (oauth_clients), not a conversation or feed — surface via existing /api/{org}/clients, not derived audit rows"
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: project

9	---
10	
11	Decided 2026-07-27 after building the wrong thing twice and having codex refute it.
12	
13	**The model.** An MCP client is **connection-shaped**, not conversation-shaped and
14	not feed-shaped:
15	- `oauth_clients` row already = credential + status + revoke → a connection.
16	- NOT a feed: `feeds` is a scheduled PULL (`schedule`, `next_run_at`, `checkpoint`,
17	  `items_collected`). MCP is push-driven; those columns would be meaningless.
18	- NOT a conversation: the MCP tool path has ZERO `conversationId` references, and
19	  `agent_transcript_snapshot.run_id` is NOT NULL (worker-only), so there is no
20	  transcript to open.
21	
22	**The surface already exists and had no page:** `GET /api/{org}/clients`
23	(`packages/server/src/lobu/client-routes.ts:197`) returns MCP + messaging clients
24	with status/authState/lastSeenAt/assignedAgentId/capabilities, plus
25	`DELETE /mcp/:clientId` to revoke. `useConnectedClients` (owletto
26	`src/lib/api/clients.ts`) is typed and consumed in exactly ONE place (a
27	behavior-builder panel).
28	
29	**Where it goes: under RUNTIME, not a new top-level page.**
30	`packages/owletto/src/app/$owner/infrastructure/` already holds devices, models,
31	sandboxes, deployments — "things attached to the workspace that do work". An MCP
32	client is the same category as a device. Mirror `infrastructure/devices/`
33	(`index.tsx` + `$deviceId.tsx`, data via `useDevices` with
34	`refetchInterval: 60000` — reuse that cadence, no need to invent one). NOT under
35	connectors (those are credentialed integrations you configure) and NOT in Recent
36	(Recent is ACTIVITY; runtime is INVENTORY). The client's activity is the
37	`client_id`-filtered events drill-down FROM its detail page.
38	
39	**Why the derived-audit approach was wrong** (deleted, do not retry):
40	- `recordToolInvocationAudit` → `buildPayload` only instruments **`run_sdk` and
41	  `query_sql`**; every other tool returns null and writes NOTHING
42	  (`tools/audit.ts` ~line 56-101). So audit events are a PARTIAL log, never
43	  "everything a client did".
44	- Deriving a client inventory from events is wrong in both directions: a client
45	  with no qualifying event disappears; a REVOKED client with old events persists.
46	- `client_name` is not a stable identity (prod: 6 client_ids for "Lobu CLI", 18
47	  registrations → 6 names). Group only in the clients API with explicit canonical
48	  identity + explicit multi-registration revoke semantics.
49	
50	**Recent sidebar caveat.** Recent IS a union (behaviors are listed with no
51	`conversations` row), so "not a conversation" alone does not disqualify an entry.
52	But `useRecentAgentThreads` fans out `scope:"all"` **once per agent** and
53	concatenates with no cross-agent dedup — so any ORG-GLOBAL row emitted from the
54	agent-scoped `listAgentThreads` duplicates once per agent. Behaviors are safe
55	because they are genuinely agent-scoped. Verified by reproduction: 2 agents →
56	`["mcp_Lobu CLI","mcp_Lobu CLI"]`.
57	
58	**State as of 2026-07-27 (PR #2211 OPEN, worktree `.claude/worktrees/mcp-read-path`,
59	branch `feat/mcp-read-path`, clean tree).** Commits on the branch:
60	- `b2093a0ee` events `client_id` filter — **KEEP**, the only sound piece
61	- `89010a702` + `a1c3de320` derived MCP sidebar — **DELETE** (reproduced broken)
62	- `bc6b0d629` / `b4a12bb60` / `fc6eaa168` submodule churn — **DELETE**; a
63	  codesmith bot repointed owletto to main mid-PR and silently dropped the sidebar
64	  commit from the diff (merge, don't rebase, on submodule branches)
65	
66	**Plan.** PR 1: keep the filter, delete the derived work, fix the score-path hole
67	for BOTH `client_ids` and `agent_id` (one pre-existing class). PR 2:
68	`infrastructure/clients` mirroring `devices/`.
69	
70	**Asked 2026-07-27: "should an MCP client show as a connector too? group under
71	the feed for all conversations?"** Answer: no to both at the SCHEMA level, yes to
72	the unifying instinct at the PAGE level.
73	- `connections` and `oauth_clients` have **no FK in either direction** — verified
74	  against the live schema. They were never linked, so this is not two drifted
75	  views of one thing. `connections.connector_key` is NOT NULL and there is no
76	  MCP connector definition in `packages/connectors/`; forcing one means inventing
77	  a fake connector_key + a fake connection row per registration, kept in sync
78	  forever. A connector reaches OUT (you configure creds); an MCP client registers
79	  itself to reach IN.
80	- Not a feed: `feeds` has `schedule`, `next_run_at`, `checkpoint`,
81	  `items_collected` — all NULL forever for push-driven MCP.
82	- The right unification is ONE PAGE (`infrastructure/`, alongside devices),
83	  not one table. Consistent with [[feedback_dont_overconsolidate_surfaces]].
84	
85	**RESOLVED 2026-07-27 (both, decided from the code, not preference):**
86	1. **Authz.** `mcpAuth` only resolves identity — it does NOT authorize a role
87	   (`middleware.ts` is a one-line delegate to `resolveAuth`). Revoke is now
88	   owner/admin via a `withOrgAdmin` wrapper; LIST stays open to members (no
89	   secrets, and hiding it defeats a page whose job is spotting a rogue client).
90	   Elevated == owner|admin to match `resolveToolAccessLevel`.
91	   **BEHAVIOR CHANGE:** members now get 403 on
92	   `DELETE /api/{org}/clients/mcp/:clientId`. This broke a real pre-existing
93	   test (`integration/mcp/auth.test.ts`) whose fixture user joins as `member` —
94	   proof the gate bites. `memberRole` IS populated for org-scoped requests
95	   (multi-tenant.ts reads the `member` table, cached — invalidate with
96	   `invalidateMembershipRoleCache`).
97	2. **Multi-registration.** Revoke operates on ONE `client_id`, so "revoke
98	   ChatGPT" left the other 5 registrations live. Added opt-in `?scope=all`
99	   fanning out across same `(client_name, user_id, organization_id)`; default
100	   stays single-id so existing callers are unchanged. The UI always sends
101	   `scope=all` because its row represents the APP.
102	   Grouping is done in the PAGE (display-only), not the API — changing the API
103	   shape would break its existing behavior-builder consumer. Group key includes
104	   the linked user so one person's Revoke can't disconnect another's client.
105	
106	**Gotcha:** there is NO `/$owner/events` route — events live under
107	`/$owner/memory` with a permissive `pruneSearch`. A "view this client's
108	activity" deep link needs the memory scope-bar filter wiring; deliberately left
109	out rather than shipped broken.
110	
111	**REVERSED IN PART 2026-07-28 — headless positioning promotes MCP activity into
112	Recent.** New premise: Lobu is positioned headless, so MCP clients (ChatGPT,
113	Claude, CLI) are the PRIMARY traffic and the web app is their observability
114	console — a Recent that shows only web chats hides the product's main usage. The
115	2026-07-27 mechanical objections were valid and are being FIXED, not dismissed:
116	- "audit is partial" → one-function fix: `recordToolInvocationAudit` already runs
117	  on EVERY tool call at the single dispatch seam (`tools/execute.ts` ~262/276);
118	  only `buildPayload` discards non-run_sdk/query_sql tools. Add a generic
119	  fallback payload.
120	- "not conversation-shaped" → MCP sessions have persistent identity
121	  (`McpSessionStore`, replica-surviving). Group audit events by session →
122	  session-shaped Recent entry ("ChatGPT — 14 calls, 1 pending approval").
123	- dedup bug → never architectural; MCP activity is org-global, must come from an
124	  org-level endpoint, NOT the per-agent `listAgentThreads` fanout (the deleted
125	  `89010a702` approach — still do not retry that topology).
126	Sequence agreed: (1) approval-chain fix FIRST (occurred_at default + ACL
127	resource gate exempting interaction events — a pending approval invisible at
128	`/{org}/memory?run_ids=` is the sharpest headless failure; found 2026-07-28:
129	`compileResourceVisibility` hides empty-entity_ids approval events on
130	ACL-enforced connections from EVERYONE); (2) complete audit coverage + stamp
131	session id + occurred_at; (3) org-level Recent arm grouped by MCP session;
132	(4) `infrastructure/clients` page demoted to inventory/revoke (trust surface).
133	
134	**Step 1 SHIPPED** lobu#2229 (2026-07-28, deployed + live-verified: run 757649's
135	approval card renders at `/lobu-team/memory?run_ids=757649`).
136	**Step 2 SHIPPED** lobu#2233 (2026-07-28): every oauth/pat tool call audited;
137	`mcp_session_id` in audit metadata (stamped at `onsessioninitialized`; recovery
138	path reuses the id via its sessionIdGenerator); `org_slug` recorded on query_sql
139	audit rows. **Audit content contract (survived 8 review rounds — do not weaken):
140	generic entries persist call SHAPE only.** Values → sentinel except
141	booleans/null; property names survive only if schema-declared at top level
142	(audit fires on FAILED validation too, so even enum keys can carry pasted
143	secrets); error = name/code only, never handler message text; args_sha256 over
144	the sanitized JSON (raw hash = offline credential verifier). Pattern redaction
145	(header-credential eats full value; Digest param lists) still guards
146	run_sdk/query_sql previews. Declined-with-rationale: auditing DENIED calls
147	(checkToolAccess pre-seam) is a separate auth-audit feature.
148	**org_slug "silent rescope" was a FALSE POSITIVE** (2026-07-28, live-verified):
149	the redirect works; the audit row records the BOUND org, which misled two
150	sessions — fixed by recording org_slug in the payload.
151	**Step 3 server half SHIPPED** lobu#2239 (2026-07-28):
152	`GET /api/{org}/clients/sessions` — audit ledger grouped by mcp_session_id
153	(client name via oauth_clients join, call/failure counts, tools as
154	to_jsonb(text[]) for the fetch_types:false client, 14-day window), exact
155	pendingInteractionCount via `metadata.mcp_session_id` now stamped on ALL FOUR
156	approval-emitting sites (manage_operations, manage_agents, manage_behaviors,
157	entity-field-approval — review-fix generalized my single-site stamp).
158	**PLACEMENT DECIDED 2026-07-28 (user):** NO separate infrastructure/clients
159	page — clients render as a section of the CONNECTORS surface (owletto#614 made
160	connectors the site map), each client app as a connection-style card, activity

---
name: project_mcp_client_activity_surface
description: "MCP client activity is a CONNECTION (oauth_clients), not a conversation or feed — surface via existing /api/{org}/clients, not derived audit rows"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 830d2806-d323-48b7-80b9-f28cf7556caf
  modified: 2026-07-28T07:31:35.912Z
---

Decided 2026-07-27 after building the wrong thing twice and having codex refute it.

**The model.** An MCP client is **connection-shaped**, not conversation-shaped and
not feed-shaped:
- `oauth_clients` row already = credential + status + revoke → a connection.
- NOT a feed: `feeds` is a scheduled PULL (`schedule`, `next_run_at`, `checkpoint`,
  `items_collected`). MCP is push-driven; those columns would be meaningless.
- NOT a conversation: the MCP tool path has ZERO `conversationId` references, and
  `agent_transcript_snapshot.run_id` is NOT NULL (worker-only), so there is no
  transcript to open.

**The surface already exists and had no page:** `GET /api/{org}/clients`
(`packages/server/src/lobu/client-routes.ts:197`) returns MCP + messaging clients
with status/authState/lastSeenAt/assignedAgentId/capabilities, plus
`DELETE /mcp/:clientId` to revoke. `useConnectedClients` (owletto
`src/lib/api/clients.ts`) is typed and consumed in exactly ONE place (a
behavior-builder panel).

**Where it goes: under RUNTIME, not a new top-level page.**
`packages/owletto/src/app/$owner/infrastructure/` already holds devices, models,
sandboxes, deployments — "things attached to the workspace that do work". An MCP
client is the same category as a device. Mirror `infrastructure/devices/`
(`index.tsx` + `$deviceId.tsx`, data via `useDevices` with
`refetchInterval: 60000` — reuse that cadence, no need to invent one). NOT under
connectors (those are credentialed integrations you configure) and NOT in Recent
(Recent is ACTIVITY; runtime is INVENTORY). The client's activity is the
`client_id`-filtered events drill-down FROM its detail page.

**Why the derived-audit approach was wrong** (deleted, do not retry):
- `recordToolInvocationAudit` → `buildPayload` only instruments **`run_sdk` and
  `query_sql`**; every other tool returns null and writes NOTHING
  (`tools/audit.ts` ~line 56-101). So audit events are a PARTIAL log, never
  "everything a client did".
- Deriving a client inventory from events is wrong in both directions: a client
  with no qualifying event disappears; a REVOKED client with old events persists.
- `client_name` is not a stable identity (prod: 6 client_ids for "Lobu CLI", 18
  registrations → 6 names). Group only in the clients API with explicit canonical
  identity + explicit multi-registration revoke semantics.

**Recent sidebar caveat.** Recent IS a union (behaviors are listed with no
`conversations` row), so "not a conversation" alone does not disqualify an entry.
But `useRecentAgentThreads` fans out `scope:"all"` **once per agent** and
concatenates with no cross-agent dedup — so any ORG-GLOBAL row emitted from the
agent-scoped `listAgentThreads` duplicates once per agent. Behaviors are safe
because they are genuinely agent-scoped. Verified by reproduction: 2 agents →
`["mcp_Lobu CLI","mcp_Lobu CLI"]`.

**State as of 2026-07-27 (PR #2211 OPEN, worktree `.claude/worktrees/mcp-read-path`,
branch `feat/mcp-read-path`, clean tree).** Commits on the branch:
- `b2093a0ee` events `client_id` filter — **KEEP**, the only sound piece
- `89010a702` + `a1c3de320` derived MCP sidebar — **DELETE** (reproduced broken)
- `bc6b0d629` / `b4a12bb60` / `fc6eaa168` submodule churn — **DELETE**; a
  codesmith bot repointed owletto to main mid-PR and silently dropped the sidebar
  commit from the diff (merge, don't rebase, on submodule branches)

**Plan.** PR 1: keep the filter, delete the derived work, fix the score-path hole
for BOTH `client_ids` and `agent_id` (one pre-existing class). PR 2:
`infrastructure/clients` mirroring `devices/`.

**Asked 2026-07-27: "should an MCP client show as a connector too? group under
the feed for all conversations?"** Answer: no to both at the SCHEMA level, yes to
the unifying instinct at the PAGE level.
- `connections` and `oauth_clients` have **no FK in either direction** — verified
  against the live schema. They were never linked, so this is not two drifted
  views of one thing. `connections.connector_key` is NOT NULL and there is no
  MCP connector definition in `packages/connectors/`; forcing one means inventing
  a fake connector_key + a fake connection row per registration, kept in sync
  forever. A connector reaches OUT (you configure creds); an MCP client registers
  itself to reach IN.
- Not a feed: `feeds` has `schedule`, `next_run_at`, `checkpoint`,
  `items_collected` — all NULL forever for push-driven MCP.
- The right unification is ONE PAGE (`infrastructure/`, alongside devices),
  not one table. Consistent with [[feedback_dont_overconsolidate_surfaces]].

**RESOLVED 2026-07-27 (both, decided from the code, not preference):**
1. **Authz.** `mcpAuth` only resolves identity — it does NOT authorize a role
   (`middleware.ts` is a one-line delegate to `resolveAuth`). Revoke is now
   owner/admin via a `withOrgAdmin` wrapper; LIST stays open to members (no
   secrets, and hiding it defeats a page whose job is spotting a rogue client).
   Elevated == owner|admin to match `resolveToolAccessLevel`.
   **BEHAVIOR CHANGE:** members now get 403 on
   `DELETE /api/{org}/clients/mcp/:clientId`. This broke a real pre-existing
   test (`integration/mcp/auth.test.ts`) whose fixture user joins as `member` —
   proof the gate bites. `memberRole` IS populated for org-scoped requests
   (multi-tenant.ts reads the `member` table, cached — invalidate with
   `invalidateMembershipRoleCache`).
2. **Multi-registration.** Revoke operates on ONE `client_id`, so "revoke
   ChatGPT" left the other 5 registrations live. Added opt-in `?scope=all`
   fanning out across same `(client_name, user_id, organization_id)`; default
   stays single-id so existing callers are unchanged. The UI always sends
   `scope=all` because its row represents the APP.
   Grouping is done in the PAGE (display-only), not the API — changing the API
   shape would break its existing behavior-builder consumer. Group key includes
   the linked user so one person's Revoke can't disconnect another's client.

**Gotcha:** there is NO `/$owner/events` route — events live under
`/$owner/memory` with a permissive `pruneSearch`. A "view this client's
activity" deep link needs the memory scope-bar filter wiring; deliberately left
out rather than shipped broken.

**REVERSED IN PART 2026-07-28 — headless positioning promotes MCP activity into
Recent.** New premise: Lobu is positioned headless, so MCP clients (ChatGPT,
Claude, CLI) are the PRIMARY traffic and the web app is their observability
console — a Recent that shows only web chats hides the product's main usage. The
2026-07-27 mechanical objections were valid and are being FIXED, not dismissed:
- "audit is partial" → one-function fix: `recordToolInvocationAudit` already runs
  on EVERY tool call at the single dispatch seam (`tools/execute.ts` ~262/276);
  only `buildPayload` discards non-run_sdk/query_sql tools. Add a generic
  fallback payload.
- "not conversation-shaped" → MCP sessions have persistent identity
  (`McpSessionStore`, replica-surviving). Group audit events by session →
  session-shaped Recent entry ("ChatGPT — 14 calls, 1 pending approval").
- dedup bug → never architectural; MCP activity is org-global, must come from an
  org-level endpoint, NOT the per-agent `listAgentThreads` fanout (the deleted
  `89010a702` approach — still do not retry that topology).
Sequence agreed: (1) approval-chain fix FIRST (occurred_at default + ACL
resource gate exempting interaction events — a pending approval invisible at
`/{org}/memory?run_ids=` is the sharpest headless failure; found 2026-07-28:
`compileResourceVisibility` hides empty-entity_ids approval events on
ACL-enforced connections from EVERYONE); (2) complete audit coverage + stamp
session id + occurred_at; (3) org-level Recent arm grouped by MCP session;
(4) `infrastructure/clients` page demoted to inventory/revoke (trust surface).

**Step 1 SHIPPED** lobu#2229 (2026-07-28, deployed + live-verified: run 757649's
approval card renders at `/lobu-team/memory?run_ids=757649`).
**Step 2 SHIPPED** lobu#2233 (2026-07-28): every oauth/pat tool call audited;
`mcp_session_id` in audit metadata (stamped at `onsessioninitialized`; recovery
path reuses the id via its sessionIdGenerator); `org_slug` recorded on query_sql
audit rows. **Audit content contract (survived 8 review rounds — do not weaken):
generic entries persist call SHAPE only.** Values → sentinel except
booleans/null; property names survive only if schema-declared at top level
(audit fires on FAILED validation too, so even enum keys can carry pasted
secrets); error = name/code only, never handler message text; args_sha256 over
the sanitized JSON (raw hash = offline credential verifier). Pattern redaction
(header-credential eats full value; Digest param lists) still guards
run_sdk/query_sql previews. Declined-with-rationale: auditing DENIED calls
(checkToolAccess pre-seam) is a separate auth-audit feature.
**org_slug "silent rescope" was a FALSE POSITIVE** (2026-07-28, live-verified):
the redirect works; the audit row records the BOUND org, which misled two
sessions — fixed by recording org_slug in the payload.
**Step 3 server half SHIPPED** lobu#2239 (2026-07-28):
`GET /api/{org}/clients/sessions` — audit ledger grouped by mcp_session_id
(client name via oauth_clients join, call/failure counts, tools as
to_jsonb(text[]) for the fetch_types:false client, 14-day window), exact
pendingInteractionCount via `metadata.mcp_session_id` now stamped on ALL FOUR
approval-emitting sites (manage_operations, manage_agents, manage_behaviors,
entity-field-approval — review-fix generalized my single-site stamp).
**PLACEMENT DECIDED 2026-07-28 (user):** NO separate infrastructure/clients
page — clients render as a section of the CONNECTORS surface (owletto#614 made
connectors the site map), each client app as a connection-style card, activity
feed-LIKE from filtered events. Schema stays split: no fake connections rows,
no feeds rows (pull-only columns) — page-level unification only.
**Step 4 SHIPPED 2026-07-28 — program COMPLETE.** owletto#603 (squashed
`260a9861`) + lobu#2219 (squashed `2e505295e`) merged:
- Connected apps page at `/$owner/connectors/apps` (one row per APP via
  server-side `registrationGroupKey`; admin-gated Revoke always sends
  `scope=all`; load-failure state).
- "Client apps" filter on the home activity timeline (one row per MCP SESSION
  from `/clients/sessions`: counts, tool summary, amber pending-approvals
  badge, links to the apps page).
- Owner-scoped revocation: `revokeClientForOrganization(clientId, orgId,

  Display/revoke/sibling picks all use identical LIVE-GRANT-FIRST ordering

  from the token, never COALESCE with `oc.user_id`. Tokenless org-owned
  registrations stay visible as disconnected (LEFT JOIN LATERAL, not INNER).
- Update-only session RECOVERY: recovery now uses `refreshSession` (update-only)

  404 re-initialize. Both races (established-session refresh AND recovery)
  are pinned by deterministic tests.
- Mutation-proven session test: revoking the displayed owner of a shared
  registration keeps the coworker's live session working across a simulated
  pod restart (auth.test.ts); dropping the userId scope makes it fail.
**OWED: post-deploy prod verify** (Flux ~30-60min): ChatGPT session appears in
`/clients/sessions` with pending count; `/{org}/connectors/apps` renders;
Client apps filter works.
**Deferred follow-ups:** session cards in the "all" activity filter need a
server-side `list_activity` arm (attention ordering); deep-link from session
row to client-filtered memory view needs memory scope-bar wiring.

merged carrying the pin to 93a493ae; standalone-bump attempts #2237/#2238
closed — a pin bump without paired parent code breaks the frontend build

input.sql:
SELECT e.created_at, e.metadata->>'tool_name' AS tool, jsonb_array_length(COALESCE(e.payload_data->'sdk_call_trace','[]'::jsonb)) AS trace_len, e.payload_data->'sdk_call_trace'->0->>'path' AS first_path, e.payload_data->>'request_status' AS request_status, left(e.payload_data->>'script_preview_redacted', 120) AS script_preview
FROM events e WHERE e.client_id = 'REDACTED' AND e.metadata->>'tool_name' = 'run_sdk'
ORDER BY e.created_at DESC LIMIT 3

content.text:
Yes — every MCP tool call from an external client is stored, on two write paths.

**1. Append-only audit event per call** (`packages/server/src/tools/execute.ts:248,304,323` → `recordToolInvocationAudit`, `packages/server/src/tools/audit.ts:255`). It fires at the single dispatch seam on both success and failure, writing an `events` row with `origin_type='tool_invocation'`, `semantic_type=AUDIT_SEMANTIC_TYPE`, `client_id` = the OAuth client, and metadata `{tool_name, token_type, agent_id, mcp_session_id, mcp_conversation_id}`.

What's in the payload depends on the tool:
- `run_sdk` / `query_sdk` / `query_sql` (`REQUEST_EVENT_TOOLS`) — the **exact request args** (`request_status:'complete'`, up to 256 KB), plus `script_sha256`, a redaction-passed `script_preview_redacted` / `sql_preview_redacted`, `sdk_call_count`, the full **`sdk_call_trace`** (each SDK path + args), `side_effect_preview`, duration, error.
- every other tool — call **shape only**: `args_sha256` + `args_preview_redacted` over sanitized args (values sentineled except booleans/null; keys survive only if schema-declared), success/error name, duration. That generic arm is deliberately gated to `tokenType` of `oauth` or `pat` (`audit.ts:218-224`) — browser-session and anonymous generic reads write nothing.

**2. Rolled-up conversation row** (`recordMcpConversationActivity`, `packages/server/src/lobu/stores/mcp-client-conversations.ts:73`) — upserts `mcp_client_conversations` keyed `(organization_id, client_identity, conversation_id)` with `call_count`, `failed_count`, `tools[]`, `last_action`, `transport_session_ids`, `last_activity_at`. This is the write-time materialization behind `/api/{org}/clients/sessions`, the `/{org}/connectors/apps` page, and the "Client apps" activity filter.

**Live on prod right now** (audited calls per registration):

```
Lobu CLI    110,964 + 5,629 + 2,562 + 1,567 …   last 2026-08-05T11:51Z
Claude        3,806                              last 2026-08-03
ChatGPT       2,179                              last 2026-08-04T22:20Z
Codex           463 + 124
Owletto for Mac  19 + 4
```

ChatGPT's latest `run_sdk` rows carry `request_status=complete`, a readable script preview, and a `sdk_call_trace` with `path=operations.execute` — so the actual SDK call is recoverable, not just the tool name. PAT-auth calls are stored too (`query_sdk` 447, `run_sdk` 296) but with `client_id` NULL, since there's no OAuth client to attribute them to.

Confidence: **high (90)** on the storage claim — read the current write path in `audit.ts` / `execute.ts` and confirmed it against live prod rows via `query_sql`, including payload contents. Lower (70) on the `mcp_client_conversations` rollup being complete in prod: that table isn't in the MCP query allowlist, so I verified the code path but not its live rows.

Next actions you could pick from:
- Query the rollup directly against the prod DB (psql) to confirm `mcp_client_conversations` matches the event counts above.
- Decide whether the generic-arm gate should also cover browser-session calls — today web-app tool use leaves no audit row.
- Check whether `conversations.client_id` is still missing (memory flags it as the attribution gap that lumps ChatGPT/Claude/CLI/web into one bucket).

content.text:
Because the request body is deliberately gated on the read path — it's stored, but four separate things have to line up before the UI can render it, and in the normal Activity view none of them do.

**1. Every list/search read strips it, unconditionally.** `hydrateToolInvocationRequests` (`packages/server/src/tools/get_content/render.ts:40`) deletes `request` / `request_status` / `request_bytes` from *every* audit item first, and only puts them back when `restoreRequests` is true. That flag is `isExactIdRead` — `Boolean(args.content_ids?.length)` (`get_content/handler.ts:439,655`). So scrolling `/{org}/activity` or `/{org}/memory` can never show it; only a read that names the event id can.

**2. Even on an exact-id read, you must be the author or an admin.** `if (!isAdmin && row.created_by !== userId) continue` (`render.ts:73,85`). `created_by` is the user the OAuth token is linked to, so another member's ChatGPT calls stay closed to you unless you're owner/admin.

**3. There is no in-app click that produces an exact-id read for these rows.** `peekHref` is only built when `content.run_id != null` (`event-card.tsx:1807`) — audit events have no run, so the card is inert by design. The `Request` disclosure button does exist (`event-card.tsx:2094`, gated on `auditPayload.request !== undefined`), but nothing in the UI navigates you to the URL that would populate it. You have to hand-write `/{org}/memory?content_ids=<event_id>`.

**4. `query_sql` never returns it at all.** `table-schema.ts:366-380` projects `payload_data - 'request'` for audit rows, since that path has no per-row caller gate. That's why my earlier query could show you `request_status=complete` but not the script itself.

There's a fifth trap if the page falls through to the anonymous route: `/api/{org}/public/knowledge/search` builds `publicToolContext` with `userId: null, memberRole: null` (`rest-api.ts:83-103`), which short-circuits the restore at `render.ts:73` regardless of `content_ids`. The signed-in hook goes through `apiCall('read_knowledge', …)` instead (`packages/owletto/src/lib/api/content.ts:116`), which does carry your identity — so which hook the page mounted decides whether the gate is even reachable.

Quick way to test on yourself: take one of your own `run_sdk` rows and open `/{org}/memory?content_ids=<id>` — the `Request` button should appear with the verbatim args. Note `request_status` can also be `too_large` (>256 KB) or `unavailable`, and only `run_sdk` / `query_sdk` / `query_sql` retain a request at all; every other tool stores shape only, so there is genuinely nothing to show for them.

Confidence: **85** on the read-path chain — traced all four gates in current source and confirmed the strip in `query_sql` against live prod (`request_status` visible, `request` absent). Not verified: I did not load the page as your browser session, so I haven't confirmed which of gates 3/5 is the one actually biting you.

Next actions you could pick from:
- Open `/{org}/memory?content_ids=<one of your run_sdk event ids>` and check whether the `Request` button renders — that separates "no route to the exact-id read" (gate 3) from "identity never reaches the gate" (gate 5).
- If it renders, the fix is small: make audit cards peekable via `content_ids` instead of requiring `run_id`, so the client-session drill-down lands on a page that can show the body.
- Decide whether admins should get requests inline in a `client_id`-filtered view — that's a policy change to gate 1, not a bug.

aiTitle: Review SDK call storage for MCP clients

content.text:
Tested it end-to-end in your real Chrome (connection 432, DOM reads, tab closed after). It works — and there's no encryption anywhere in this path.

**Test 1 — exact-id read as you.** `https://app.lobu.ai/buremba/memory?content_ids=4816515` (redirects to `/buremba/activity?content_ids=…`, param preserved). The `Request` button renders, and clicking it expands the verbatim body:

```
Request
{ "script": "\nexport default async (ctx, client) => {\n  const ops = await client.operations.listAvailable({ connection_id: 432, include_disconnected: true });\n  return (ops.operations ?? ops ?? []).map(o => o.operation_key ?? o.key);\n};" }
Category audit · Event type tool_invocation.completed · Token type oauth · Tool name run_sdk
```

**Test 2 — the same page without `content_ids`.** `/buremba/activity` renders 57 buttons, **0** of them `Request`. That's the strip working as designed, and it's why it looked to you like nothing is stored.

I also hit the same gate through the SDK (`knowledge.read({content_ids:[4816404, 4816515]})`) and both payloads came back with `request` + `request_status:"complete"` — the verbatim SQL and the verbatim script.

One caveat on "as owner": every one of the 128,975 audit rows in `buremba` has `created_by` = you, so this test only exercised the **author** arm of the gate. The admin arm (`isAdminOrOwnerRole` letting you read a *coworker's* request) is untested — there's no foreign-authored row on prod to test it with.

**On encryption: there is none, and nothing here is encrypted-at-rest beyond the DB itself.** What you're seeing is three cheaper mechanisms, and only one of them is arguably excessive:

- `script_sha256` / `sql_sha256` / `args_sha256` — identity hashes for dedupe, not protection. Keep.
- `*_preview_redacted` — pattern redaction over a 500-char preview. Defensible, because the preview is visible to *all* members in list views while the verbatim `request` is author/admin-only. Two audiences, two fidelities.
- `sanitizeArgLeaves` on non-`run_sdk`/`query_sql`/`query_sdk` tools — **this is the over-redaction.** Live example from your 54k `manage_operations` rows:

  ```
  {"limit":"__LOBU_REDACTED__","action":"__LOBU_REDACTED__"}
  ```

  `action` is a schema-declared enum. Hiding `"list"` protects nothing, and the result is that the highest-volume tool in your workspace records literally no usable information. The asymmetry is stark: `run_sdk` keeps an entire arbitrary script verbatim, while `manage_operations` won't admit it was a list call.

The original rationale (in the code comment at `audit.ts:71-84`) is real — audit fires on *failed* validation too, so a value typed as an enum can be arbitrary pasted text. But that's fixable narrowly instead of by blanket sentinel: at audit time, keep the value only if it **matches a declared enum member**. A value that equals one of N compile-time constants is provably not a secret. Same for booleans/null, which already survive. Free-text and identifier-shaped values stay sentineled.

Confidence: **95** on "the owner path works" — exercised in your real browser and via the SDK, both arms of the list/exact-id contrast confirmed. **70** on the admin arm — code reads correctly (`render.ts:85`) but no prod data exists to test it. **90** on "no encryption, one over-redaction" — read the full write path; the only transforms are hash, regex-redact, sentinel.

Next actions you could pick from:
- Relax the generic sanitizer to enum-match (small, contained change to `sanitizeArgLeaves` + `schemaPropertyNames`) so `manage_operations` rows say what action ran.
- Make audit cards peekable by `content_ids` instead of requiring `run_id` (`event-card.tsx:1807`) — today there is no click anywhere in the app that reaches the request body; you have to type the URL.
- Add a member fixture in `buremba` (or a staging org) to actually prove the admin arm of the gate, since it's the half that carries the privacy risk.
- Consider whether the "Client apps" session rows should deep-link to the client-filtered activity view — that's the discoverability gap behind your original question.

<!-- Per-repo agent rules loaded into every Claude Code session in this repo. Inlines AGENTS.md (shared project rules) first, then layers local-only notes below. User memory entries live under ~/.claude/projects/.../memory/. Don't add anything here unless it's only relevant to Claude agent specific. If other harnesses like pi or codex need it, modify AGENTS.md -->

@AGENTS.md

content.content:
## Repo map
- Bun workspace under `packages/*`; TS source is in `src`, tests in `__tests__`.
- Main packages: `core` shared types/utils, `plugin-api` native plugin contracts, `plugin-host` deterministic plugin composition, `server` gateway + embedded runtime, `agent-worker` Lobu agent execution, `connectors` built-in connectors, `owletto` frontend submodule.
- Before editing a package, read its nearest `AGENTS.md` if present.
- `docs/GOTCHAS.md` collects the mechanical traps (build, SQL, testing, submodule, browser) that have each cost a debugging session. Skim the section for the surface you are touching before you start, and grep it when something looks inexplicable.

## Hard invariants
- **Never write to `~/Code/lobu` directly — work in a worktree.** Run `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` first, and never `git switch` in the main checkout.
- One branch = one concern (not one file). Tangential task → commit/push/open current work, then branch fresh from `main`. Split only for genuinely independent concerns or an unreviewable diff.
- **Multi-replica correctness is mandatory.** Never put shared required state in an in-memory Map/singleton another replica must read or mutate. If a feature relies on cross-pod visibility, use Postgres-mediated state/signal.
- **`events` is append-only.** Never `DELETE FROM events`; tombstone/supersede instead.
- **`events.id` is a stored-version id, not stable source identity.** Connector resyncs can supersede a row and allocate a new id for the same source item. Cross-sync identity and dedupe must use the connector's stable `origin_id` (scoped to its connection/source) or an explicit domain key, never `events.id`.
- **Request paths never aggregate history.** No `GROUP BY`, `DISTINCT ON`, per-row `regexp_*`, or leading-wildcard `LIKE` over an append-only / run-history table (`events`, `agent_transcript_snapshot`, `session_calls`, …) on a user-facing read path. History only grows, so read-time aggregation cost grows with it while the answer stays bounded. Materialize the row or counter at WRITE time and read it back by index; run the one-time aggregation in a migration, never per request. Aggregating bounded config tables (`connections`, `watchers`, `agent_users`) is fine.
- **Never bulk-delete prod `organization` rows**, including zero-activity ones — empty-looking orgs are frequently real human signups. Surface them one at a time for confirmation.
- **Workers never receive real credentials.** They may receive only placeholders/proxied access. The only exceptions are device-pinned connectors and short-lived provider-derived credential leases (see `packages/server/AGENTS.md`); a durable stored credential is never one of them.
- Default to static `import`. New dynamic imports require measured cost justification here or in the package AGENTS plus a rationale comment at the call site. Tests may dynamically import after mocks.
  - Node-version gate exceptions: `packages/cli/bin/lobu.js` defers the existing CLI graph without duplicating it, and `packages/server/src/server-entry.ts` adds an 842-byte gate in front of the 4.34 MB server graph (measured 2026-07-24). Both call sites must stay dependency-free until their checks pass.
- Bug fixes require red→fix→green evidence, with both outputs pasted into the PR body. If you cannot reproduce, stop and report the dead end — do not ship a speculative fix.
- Mutation checks require proof that the mutation landed: assert the old pattern exists, verify a countable source change, and confirm the focused test fails before restoring the fix and rerunning green. A green test after a no-op mutation proves nothing.
- Never report done off a green typecheck. Boot it, exercise every branch you touched, clean up test data. If "compiles" is all you ran, say so explicitly.
- Gates are non-negotiable (sequence in "Ship a change" below). `make pre-pr` builds first — that build step is what protects against a stale-dist false green. `make review` is an LLM verdict only: it does NOT run typecheck/knip/tests and is not proof CI will pass.
- The agent-facing product name is **Behavior**; `watcher` is internal engine/DB vocabulary. It must not appear in MCP tool schemas/names/descriptions, ClientSDK discovery metadata, or the connector-sdk public reaction contract — `make pre-pr` fails on it. Internal identifiers (`actingWatcherId`, table/column names, comments) are fine.
- `make review-fix` is the unposted fixer pass and runs BEFORE the first `make review`; verify its diff and commit it. Never iterate `make review` as a find-fix loop — each posted round costs a review + CI cycle.
- **Agents never approve their own UI proof.** For an Owletto pointer PR, `make ui-review` posts the exact approval command on the Owletto PR; only a human admin may post that command. The agent must open the linked PR, stop before merge, and rerun the gate after the human comment. A changed pointer or proof invalidates the approval.
- Fix the class, not the instance: on the first hit, grep every other instance and fix in one pass — a diff-scoped reviewer only ever finds the next one. Same root cause twice = stop reviewing, grep-enumerate. A class-wide fix is in scope for the branch that found it and does not count as scope creep.
- **Fail closed on durable dispatch/delivery state.** When a durable coordination or delivery operation fails, its caller must not reinterpret the error as proceed/deliver/skip. Propagate a retry, defer, or terminal-failure outcome with a visible log; if the operation may already have succeeded, reconcile idempotently before retrying. Treat lock timeouts, pool errors, and ambiguous or expired rows as failures, not as "nothing changed."
- **Coordination design brake.** A change that needs a second lock, a second retry/deferral budget, or a prose termination argument to explain why it halts is patching a misplaced check — stop and re-derive where the decision belongs before adding mechanism. Find the chokepoint that already serializes the action (e.g. worker dispatch is serialized by `job-router` on the worker-SSE-owner pod) and put the check there; prefer deleting the state transition over coordinating it, and reuse queue-native retry over hand-rolled hold/requeue.
- **Stage by explicit path; never commit the whole tree of a worktree that hosted other work.** A commit is a snapshot — stale file copies silently revert already-merged PRs. After commit/rebase, `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` must equal the task's intended file list; extra files = stop. Verify a "reverts merged work" review finding by diff direction against `origin/main`, never dismiss it as merge-base noise.

## Ship a change
1. `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` → work in `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/`.
2. Reproduce the bug (red) before fixing it. Fix, then prove green.
3. Test: `make test-unit` (no DB) / `make test-integration` (needs `DATABASE_URL` with pgvector). One file: `bun test <path>`, or `cd packages/server && bunx vitest run <path>` for vitest suites.
4. `make pre-pr` — build, typecheck, knip, lint, exposed-surface naming.
5. `make review-fix` on the settled diff and verify what it changed — it edits the working tree, so re-read the files before trusting them.
6. Stage by explicit path (`git add -- <paths>`, never `-A`), commit, then confirm `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` is exactly your intended file list. Extra files = stop.
7. `git push -u origin <branch>` → `gh pr create` (fill `.github/pull_request_template.md`; conventional-commit title, e.g. `fix(server): …`).
8. `make review` **once** on the settled HEAD. It posts the `pi-review` status, which is a REQUIRED check.
9. `make ui-review`. It passes non-Owletto changes as not applicable. For an Owletto pointer change, first run `ARTIFACT=<hosted-html-url> OPEN=1 make ui-review`; it posts the proof on the exact merged Owletto PR, opens that PR for the human, and leaves the required `ui-review` status pending. Stop. After the human posts the displayed `/ui-approve <sha>` comment, rerun `make ui-review` and require success.
10. Merge squash once CI is green: `gh pr merge <n> --squash --admin`. Never `--admin` past a check that has not reported.
11. Prod-visible surface? Verify it live after rollout. Set a self-rescheduling `ScheduleWakeup` (~1500s) carrying the rollout gate: poll the deployed SHA, then `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$MERGE_SHA" "$DEPLOYED_SHA"` with `MERGE_SHA=$(gh pr view <n> --json mergeCommit --jq .mergeCommit.oid)`. Two ways this gate silently never opens — **gate on the squash commit, not your branch head** (a squash merge writes a new commit with no ancestry link to the branch, so the branch head exits 1 forever: PR #2280 has identical trees and still fails), and **keep that argument order** (merge commit first; reversed, it accepts a stale deploy). Run the live check when it lands, and write the result back to memory.

## Agent workflow
- Do only what was asked. Delete ephemeral files you create. Do not create `*.md` unless asked.
- Never introduce a new table or change the database design, API surface, or SDK surface without explicitly surfacing the proposal and receiving user confirmation first.
- Prefer `bun`; do not use npm/yarn/pnpm for repo work.
- Fix unused params by deleting them, not `_`-prefixing.
- Never `git stash`; use WIP commits and squash later.
- Never resolve merge conflicts in the GitHub web UI (it has silently dropped 1000+ lines of feature work). Rebase locally against `origin/main`, then diff against the last real feature commit before squashing — except on submodule-pointer branches, where you must `git merge` (see `docs/GOTCHAS.md`, "Submodule & cross-repo").
- Run mandated gates automatically; never ask permission to run one.
- Show the diff, not a summary. Before claiming done — on your own work or a dispatched agent's — surface `git status` plus `git diff --stat <base>...HEAD`. An agent's self-report is a claim; the diff is the evidence.
- UI PRs owe before/after screenshots, and `gh` cannot upload images inline. Capture before shots from the unmodified branch and after shots from the same booted app (auth recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`), base64-embed the PNGs into one self-contained HTML comparison page, publish it as a claude.ai artifact, and pass that URL as `ARTIFACT` to `make ui-review`. The gate records it on the Owletto PR and binds human approval to the exact parent-base and Owletto-pointer pair.
- Any subagent with write access (Edit/Write/Bash) runs in its own worktree; only grep/read agents share the parent. Two writing agents must NEVER share a worktree — they overwrite each other's uncommitted work.
- Dispatch code-writing agents through `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` and brief them with the absolute `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/` path. Only task-setup does the submodule branch pinning, post-init `bun install`, `.env` copy, and port allocation.
- Do repetitive multi-file edits (renames, signature changes, import rewrites) inline or with one script. Reserve subagents for read-only breadth or genuinely isolated parallel work.
- Before adding an env var, grep for the one the codebase already reads. Do not rename existing vars to a "cleaner" convention unasked.
- Deleting code needs structural evidence (dangling import, completed migration, superseded impl). Low prod usage is not a delete signal; trace the workflow, not just the import graph — docs and help text are load-bearing too.
- **Absence is never proven by a grep on a working tree.** To prove code does *not* exist, run `git fetch -q origin && git grep <pattern> origin/main` — the fetch is load-bearing, `origin/main` itself goes stale. Applies to every existence check, including the deletion-evidence rule above.
- Slack link pasted (`slack.com/archives/…?thread_ts=`) → run `scripts/slack-thread-viewer.js "<link>"` first.
- To drive the user's real logged-in browser, use the paired Owletto extension — recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`. Do **not** assume CDP/browser-auth is required.
- Unsure in planning → ask before making conflicting or irreversible choices. Mid-execution, block on a question only for irreversible/destructive actions or decisions that are genuinely the user's; for reversible choices with a clear recommended option, take it and flag the choice in your summary.

## Session efficiency
- Never poll in the foreground (`sleep`/`until`/`while` wait loops, repeated `tail`). Run long waits (dev-server boot, CI, deploys) in the background and act on the completion notification.
- Prefer DOM reads (`get_page_text`, `read_page`, `javascript_tool`) over screenshots; screenshot only when visual layout itself is under test. Screenshots are the #1 context-bloat source.
- Read a file before editing it, and re-read it after any external change (a fixer pass, another agent, a rebase). Blind edits fail and cost a retry round-trip.
- Read PR status compactly: `gh pr view <n> --json number,title,isDraft,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision` plus `gh pr checks <n> --required`. Never `--json statusCheckRollup` — measured on PR 2280 it is 7520 bytes against 861, 8.7x larger and less legible.
- Batch narrow fixes into one commit, verified once at the end of the batch — not per fix. It never justifies skipping a reproducer or a correctness-critical test. For a one-line or config-only change, take one CI snapshot and move on.

<!-- Per-repo agent rules loaded into every Claude Code session in this repo. Inlines AGENTS.md (shared project rules) first, then layers local-only notes below. User memory entries live under ~/.claude/projects/.../memory/. Don't add anything here unless it's only relevant to Claude agent specific. If other harnesses like pi or codex need it, modify AGENTS.md -->

@AGENTS.md

content.content:
## Repo map
- Bun workspace under `packages/*`; TS source is in `src`, tests in `__tests__`.
- Main packages: `core` shared types/utils, `plugin-api` native plugin contracts, `plugin-host` deterministic plugin composition, `server` gateway + embedded runtime, `agent-worker` Lobu agent execution, `connectors` built-in connectors, `owletto` frontend submodule.
- Before editing a package, read its nearest `AGENTS.md` if present.
- `docs/GOTCHAS.md` collects the mechanical traps (build, SQL, testing, submodule, browser) that have each cost a debugging session. Skim the section for the surface you are touching before you start, and grep it when something looks inexplicable.

## Hard invariants
- **Never write to `~/Code/lobu` directly — work in a worktree.** Run `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` first, and never `git switch` in the main checkout.
- One branch = one concern (not one file). Tangential task → commit/push/open current work, then branch fresh from `main`. Split only for genuinely independent concerns or an unreviewable diff.
- **Multi-replica correctness is mandatory.** Never put shared required state in an in-memory Map/singleton another replica must read or mutate. If a feature relies on cross-pod visibility, use Postgres-mediated state/signal.
- **`events` is append-only.** Never `DELETE FROM events`; tombstone/supersede instead.
- **`events.id` is a stored-version id, not stable source identity.** Connector resyncs can supersede a row and allocate a new id for the same source item. Cross-sync identity and dedupe must use the connector's stable `origin_id` (scoped to its connection/source) or an explicit domain key, never `events.id`.
- **Request paths never aggregate history.** No `GROUP BY`, `DISTINCT ON`, per-row `regexp_*`, or leading-wildcard `LIKE` over an append-only / run-history table (`events`, `agent_transcript_snapshot`, `session_calls`, …) on a user-facing read path. History only grows, so read-time aggregation cost grows with it while the answer stays bounded. Materialize the row or counter at WRITE time and read it back by index; run the one-time aggregation in a migration, never per request. Aggregating bounded config tables (`connections`, `watchers`, `agent_users`) is fine.
- **Never bulk-delete prod `organization` rows**, including zero-activity ones — empty-looking orgs are frequently real human signups. Surface them one at a time for confirmation.
- **Workers never receive real credentials.** They may receive only placeholders/proxied access. The only exceptions are device-pinned connectors and short-lived provider-derived credential leases (see `packages/server/AGENTS.md`); a durable stored credential is never one of them.
- Default to static `import`. New dynamic imports require measured cost justification here or in the package AGENTS plus a rationale comment at the call site. Tests may dynamically import after mocks.
  - Node-version gate exceptions: `packages/cli/bin/lobu.js` defers the existing CLI graph without duplicating it, and `packages/server/src/server-entry.ts` adds an 842-byte gate in front of the 4.34 MB server graph (measured 2026-07-24). Both call sites must stay dependency-free until their checks pass.
- Bug fixes require red→fix→green evidence, with both outputs pasted into the PR body. If you cannot reproduce, stop and report the dead end — do not ship a speculative fix.
- Mutation checks require proof that the mutation landed: assert the old pattern exists, verify a countable source change, and confirm the focused test fails before restoring the fix and rerunning green. A green test after a no-op mutation proves nothing.
- Never report done off a green typecheck. Boot it, exercise every branch you touched, clean up test data. If "compiles" is all you ran, say so explicitly.
- Gates are non-negotiable (sequence in "Ship a change" below). `make pre-pr` builds first — that build step is what protects against a stale-dist false green. `make review` is an LLM verdict only: it does NOT run typecheck/knip/tests and is not proof CI will pass.
- The agent-facing product name is **Behavior**; `watcher` is internal engine/DB vocabulary. It must not appear in MCP tool schemas/names/descriptions, ClientSDK discovery metadata, or the connector-sdk public reaction contract — `make pre-pr` fails on it. Internal identifiers (`actingWatcherId`, table/column names, comments) are fine.
- `make review-fix` is the unposted fixer pass and runs BEFORE the first `make review`; verify its diff and commit it. Never iterate `make review` as a find-fix loop — each posted round costs a review + CI cycle.
- **Agents never approve their own UI proof.** For an Owletto pointer PR, `make ui-review` posts the exact approval command on the Owletto PR; only a human admin may post that command. The agent must open the linked PR, stop before merge, and rerun the gate after the human comment. A changed pointer or proof invalidates the approval.
- Fix the class, not the instance: on the first hit, grep every other instance and fix in one pass — a diff-scoped reviewer only ever finds the next one. Same root cause twice = stop reviewing, grep-enumerate. A class-wide fix is in scope for the branch that found it and does not count as scope creep.
- **Fail closed on durable dispatch/delivery state.** When a durable coordination or delivery operation fails, its caller must not reinterpret the error as proceed/deliver/skip. Propagate a retry, defer, or terminal-failure outcome with a visible log; if the operation may already have succeeded, reconcile idempotently before retrying. Treat lock timeouts, pool errors, and ambiguous or expired rows as failures, not as "nothing changed."
- **Coordination design brake.** A change that needs a second lock, a second retry/deferral budget, or a prose termination argument to explain why it halts is patching a misplaced check — stop and re-derive where the decision belongs before adding mechanism. Find the chokepoint that already serializes the action (e.g. worker dispatch is serialized by `job-router` on the worker-SSE-owner pod) and put the check there; prefer deleting the state transition over coordinating it, and reuse queue-native retry over hand-rolled hold/requeue.
- **Stage by explicit path; never commit the whole tree of a worktree that hosted other work.** A commit is a snapshot — stale file copies silently revert already-merged PRs. After commit/rebase, `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` must equal the task's intended file list; extra files = stop. Verify a "reverts merged work" review finding by diff direction against `origin/main`, never dismiss it as merge-base noise.

## Ship a change
1. `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` → work in `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/`.
2. Reproduce the bug (red) before fixing it. Fix, then prove green.
3. Test: `make test-unit` (no DB) / `make test-integration` (needs `DATABASE_URL` with pgvector). One file: `bun test <path>`, or `cd packages/server && bunx vitest run <path>` for vitest suites.
4. `make pre-pr` — build, typecheck, knip, lint, exposed-surface naming.
5. `make review-fix` on the settled diff and verify what it changed — it edits the working tree, so re-read the files before trusting them.
6. Stage by explicit path (`git add -- <paths>`, never `-A`), commit, then confirm `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` is exactly your intended file list. Extra files = stop.
7. `git push -u origin <branch>` → `gh pr create` (fill `.github/pull_request_template.md`; conventional-commit title, e.g. `fix(server): …`).
8. `make review` **once** on the settled HEAD. It posts the `pi-review` status, which is a REQUIRED check.
9. `make ui-review`. It passes non-Owletto changes as not applicable. For an Owletto pointer change, first run `ARTIFACT=<hosted-html-url> OPEN=1 make ui-review`; it posts the proof on the exact merged Owletto PR, opens that PR for the human, and leaves the required `ui-review` status pending. Stop. After the human posts the displayed `/ui-approve <sha>` comment, rerun `make ui-review` and require success.
10. Merge squash once CI is green: `gh pr merge <n> --squash --admin`. Never `--admin` past a check that has not reported.
11. Prod-visible surface? Verify it live after rollout. Set a self-rescheduling `ScheduleWakeup` (~1500s) carrying the rollout gate: poll the deployed SHA, then `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$MERGE_SHA" "$DEPLOYED_SHA"` with `MERGE_SHA=$(gh pr view <n> --json mergeCommit --jq .mergeCommit.oid)`. Two ways this gate silently never opens — **gate on the squash commit, not your branch head** (a squash merge writes a new commit with no ancestry link to the branch, so the branch head exits 1 forever: PR #2280 has identical trees and still fails), and **keep that argument order** (merge commit first; reversed, it accepts a stale deploy). Run the live check when it lands, and write the result back to memory.

## Agent workflow
- Do only what was asked. Delete ephemeral files you create. Do not create `*.md` unless asked.
- Never introduce a new table or change the database design, API surface, or SDK surface without explicitly surfacing the proposal and receiving user confirmation first.
- Prefer `bun`; do not use npm/yarn/pnpm for repo work.
- Fix unused params by deleting them, not `_`-prefixing.
- Never `git stash`; use WIP commits and squash later.
- Never resolve merge conflicts in the GitHub web UI (it has silently dropped 1000+ lines of feature work). Rebase locally against `origin/main`, then diff against the last real feature commit before squashing — except on submodule-pointer branches, where you must `git merge` (see `docs/GOTCHAS.md`, "Submodule & cross-repo").
- Run mandated gates automatically; never ask permission to run one.
- Show the diff, not a summary. Before claiming done — on your own work or a dispatched agent's — surface `git status` plus `git diff --stat <base>...HEAD`. An agent's self-report is a claim; the diff is the evidence.
- UI PRs owe before/after screenshots, and `gh` cannot upload images inline. Capture before shots from the unmodified branch and after shots from the same booted app (auth recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`), base64-embed the PNGs into one self-contained HTML comparison page, publish it as a claude.ai artifact, and pass that URL as `ARTIFACT` to `make ui-review`. The gate records it on the Owletto PR and binds human approval to the exact parent-base and Owletto-pointer pair.
- Any subagent with write access (Edit/Write/Bash) runs in its own worktree; only grep/read agents share the parent. Two writing agents must NEVER share a worktree — they overwrite each other's uncommitted work.
- Dispatch code-writing agents through `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` and brief them with the absolute `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/` path. Only task-setup does the submodule branch pinning, post-init `bun install`, `.env` copy, and port allocation.
- Do repetitive multi-file edits (renames, signature changes, import rewrites) inline or with one script. Reserve subagents for read-only breadth or genuinely isolated parallel work.
- Before adding an env var, grep for the one the codebase already reads. Do not rename existing vars to a "cleaner" convention unasked.
- Deleting code needs structural evidence (dangling import, completed migration, superseded impl). Low prod usage is not a delete signal; trace the workflow, not just the import graph — docs and help text are load-bearing too.
- **Absence is never proven by a grep on a working tree.** To prove code does *not* exist, run `git fetch -q origin && git grep <pattern> origin/main` — the fetch is load-bearing, `origin/main` itself goes stale. Applies to every existence check, including the deletion-evidence rule above.
- Slack link pasted (`slack.com/archives/…?thread_ts=`) → run `scripts/slack-thread-viewer.js "<link>"` first.
- To drive the user's real logged-in browser, use the paired Owletto extension — recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`. Do **not** assume CDP/browser-auth is required.
- Unsure in planning → ask before making conflicting or irreversible choices. Mid-execution, block on a question only for irreversible/destructive actions or decisions that are genuinely the user's; for reversible choices with a clear recommended option, take it and flag the choice in your summary.

## Session efficiency
- Never poll in the foreground (`sleep`/`until`/`while` wait loops, repeated `tail`). Run long waits (dev-server boot, CI, deploys) in the background and act on the completion notification.
- Prefer DOM reads (`get_page_text`, `read_page`, `javascript_tool`) over screenshots; screenshot only when visual layout itself is under test. Screenshots are the #1 context-bloat source.
- Read a file before editing it, and re-read it after any external change (a fixer pass, another agent, a rebase). Blind edits fail and cost a retry round-trip.
- Read PR status compactly: `gh pr view <n> --json number,title,isDraft,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision` plus `gh pr checks <n> --required`. Never `--json statusCheckRollup` — measured on PR 2280 it is 7520 bytes against 861, 8.7x larger and less legible.
- Batch narrow fixes into one commit, verified once at the end of the batch — not per fix. It never justifies skipping a reproducer or a correctness-critical test. For a one-line or config-only change, take one CI snapshot and move on.
